answer: Anchor each agent identity to a domain the agent controls. The agent registers a domain and publishes a signed TXT record proving control. The registry checks the domain is at least a year old with a continuous TLS certificate history, so a bulk buy of fresh domains fails. The agent renews the proof yearly and keeps the DNS record live, and any domain tied to two agents gets both frozen. One identity costs about $12 a year plus $60 for hosting, so to forge 1,000 sybils costs near $72,000 a year before labor. The domain is a public signal, like a shop sign anyone can walk past and check.
